recipes.name: Ring 1, long side
dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log
Length along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side
Length along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 65.54 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 0° (blade upright). Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is a square-ended block 0.50 in long. This cut meets the side of the next ring piece.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 0° (blade upright). Measure from the first cut and mark: 64.79 in along the point; 64.79 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side; 64.79 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the sawn face that lies on the open side -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a square-ended block 6.71 in long. This cut meets the side of the next ring piece.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 64.79 in along the point, 64.79 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side, 64.79 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as ring 1, long side: flipped over: sawn face against the open side, point back toward the wall.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).

Lay the rings from the frame inward. Each ring is a small frame: three pieces in the same pinwheel as the frame -- each runs from the far side of the piece behind it to the near side of the piece ahead, square-cut both ends in plan.
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
Centre: a triangle 5.1 in across its inscribed circle is left. Fill it with a plug cut from one wedge laid flat, or leave it open as a vent.
fitting: The first piece, flipped, lies flat on the frame's 45° slope: sawn face on sawn face, a full-width bearing.
Every other seam is sawn-to-sawn (tight, full face); the ones between are bark-to-bark, touching on a line, with a lens of air either side.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).

Lay the rings from the frame inward. Each ring is a small frame: three pieces in the same pinwheel as the frame -- each runs from the far side of the piece behind it to the near side of the piece ahead, square-cut both ends in plan.
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
Centre: a triangle 9.3 in across its inscribed circle is left. Fill it with a plug cut from one wedge laid flat, or leave it open as a vent.
fitting: The first piece, flipped, lies flat on the frame's 45° slope: sawn face on sawn face, a full-width bearing.
Every other seam is sawn-to-sawn (tight, full face); the ones between are bark-to-bark, touching on a line, with a lens of air either side.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
